sections.presenting_complaint: Left-sided sciatica-type leg pain for 3 weeks.
sections.history: Onset 3 weeks ago while lifting a resident at work. Pain radiates from the buttock down the posterior thigh and lateral calf into the foot; leg pain worse than back pain; up to 7/10, worse after sitting. Occasional tingling over the lateral foot. No weakness. Reports saddle numbness; no change in bladder or bowel function. No fevers. No history of cancer or unintentional weight loss. Works as a care assistant.
sections.medications_allergies: Over-the-counter ibuprofen 400 mg three times daily with little benefit. No other medications. No known drug allergies. No history of peptic ulcer, asthma or renal disease.
sections.examination: Lumbar flexion limited by pain. Straight leg raise positive on the right at 40 degrees; negative on the left. Power, reflexes and sensation normal and symmetrical in both lower limbs.
sections.impression: Right-sided sciatica, likely lumbar disc-related radiculopathy. No red flags.
sections.plan: Stop ibuprofen. Start naproxen 500 mg four times daily with food and omeprazole 20 mg once daily, for 2 weeks. Physiotherapy not required at this stage. Advised to keep active and avoid bed rest. Fit note for 2 weeks: may be fit for work with amended duties (no lifting or handling). Review in 4 weeks.
sections.safety_netting: Attend A&E immediately if saddle numbness, difficulty passing urine, loss of bladder or bowel control, or bilateral leg weakness (cauda equina symptoms). Symptom card given.
